name: Whipped Cream No. 1
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: thick sweet cream
ingredients.originalText: a pint of thick sweet cream

ingredients.name: fine white sugar
ingredients.originalText: three tablespoonfuls of fine white sugar

ingredients.name: a teaspoonful of the extract of lemon or vanilla
ingredients.originalText: a teaspoonful of the extract of lemon or vanilla
ingredients.quantityText: a teaspoonful of the extract of lemon or vanilla

instructions.text: Beat the whites of three eggs to a stiff froth
Add a pint of thick sweet cream (previously set where it is very cold)
Add four tablespoonfuls of sweet wine, three tablespoonfuls of fine white sugar and a teaspoonful of the extract of lemon or vanilla
Mix all the ingredients together on a board platter or pan
Whip it to a standing froth
As the froth rises, take it off lightly with a spoon and lay it on an inverted sieve with a dish under it to catch what will drain through
What drains through can be beaten over again
Serve in a glass dish with jelly or jam and sliced sponge cake
This should be whipped in a cool place and set in the ice box

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Beat the whites of three eggs to a stiff froth
2. Add a pint of thick sweet cream (previously set where it is very cold)
3. Add four tablespoonfuls of sweet wine, three tablespoonfuls of fine white sugar and a teaspoonful of the extract of lemon or vanilla
4. Mix all the ingredients together on a board platter or pan
5. Whip it to a standing froth
6. As the froth rises, take it off lightly with a spoon and lay it on an inverted sieve with a dish under it to catch what will drain through
7. What drains through can be beaten over again
8. Serve in a glass dish with jelly or jam and sliced sponge cake
9. This should be whipped in a cool place and set in the ice box
